knowledge_point.title: Finding an Integral That Represents the Surface Area of a Parametric Surface

question.:question/problem:
$$
\iint_D\boxed{\phantom{AAAAAAAA}}\,\mathrm dA
$$

$$
D=\{(u,v):0\le u\le 1,\ 0\le v\le 1\}
$$

The integral above gives the surface area of the parametric surface

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\langle u + v,\,4 v^{2},\,- u + v\rangle
$$

for $(u,v)\in D$.

What is the missing expression?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The surface-area integrand is the magnitude of the fundamental vector product:

$$
A(S)=\iint_D \left\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\right\|\,\mathrm dA.
$$

Differentiate each coordinate with respect to each parameter:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u&=\langle 1,\,0,\,-1\rangle \\ \mathbf r_v&=\langle 1,\,8 v,\,1\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Expand the determinant to find the cross product:

$$
\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i & \mathbf j & \mathbf k \\ 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 8 v & 1\end{vmatrix}
$$

$$
\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=\langle 8 v,\,-2,\,8 v\rangle
$$

Square the components, add, and take the nonnegative square root:

$$
\begin{aligned}\left\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\right\|^2&=\left(8 v\right)^2+\left(-2\right)^2 \\ &\quad+\left(8 v\right)^2\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\left\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\right\|&=\sqrt{128 v^{2} + 4} \\ &=\sqrt{4 \left(32 v^{2} + 1\right)} \\ &=2 \sqrt{32 v^{2} + 1}\end{aligned}
$$

Thus the required integral is

$$
A(S)=\iint_D 2 \sqrt{32 v^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm dA.
$$

The missing expression is $2 \sqrt{32 v^{2} + 1}$. The integral does not need to be evaluated.

knowledge_point.title: Finding an Integral That Represents the Surface Area of a Parametric Surface

question.:question/problem:
$$
\iint_D\boxed{\phantom{AAAAAAAA}}\,\mathrm dA
$$

$$
D=\{(u,v):0\le u\le \pi,\ 0\le v\le 4\}
$$

The integral above gives the surface area of the parametric surface

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\langle 3 v,\,e^{v} \sin{\left(u \right)},\,e^{v} \cos{\left(u \right)}\rangle
$$

for $(u,v)\in D$.

What is the missing expression?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The surface-area integrand is the magnitude of the fundamental vector product:

$$
A(S)=\iint_D \left\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\right\|\,\mathrm dA.
$$

Differentiate each coordinate with respect to each parameter:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u&=\langle 0,\,e^{v} \cos{\left(u \right)},\,- e^{v} \sin{\left(u \right)}\rangle \\ \mathbf r_v&=\langle 3,\,e^{v} \sin{\left(u \right)},\,e^{v} \cos{\left(u \right)}\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Expand the determinant to find the cross product:

$$
\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i & \mathbf j & \mathbf k \\ 0 & e^{v} \cos{\left(u \right)} & - e^{v} \sin{\left(u \right)} \\ 3 & e^{v} \sin{\left(u \right)} & e^{v} \cos{\left(u \right)}\end{vmatrix}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}c_1&=e^{2 v} \sin^{2}{\left(u \right)} + e^{2 v} \cos^{2}{\left(u \right)}=e^{2 v} \\ c_2&=- 3 e^{v} \sin{\left(u \right)} \\ c_3&=- 3 e^{v} \cos{\left(u \right)}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=\langle e^{2 v},\,- 3 e^{v} \sin{\left(u \right)},\,- 3 e^{v} \cos{\left(u \right)}\rangle
$$

Use $\sin^{2}{\left(u \right)}+\cos^{2}{\left(u \right)}=1$ to combine the squared trigonometric terms.

Square the components, add, and take the nonnegative square root:

$$
\begin{aligned}\left\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\right\|^2&=\left(e^{2 v}\right)^2+\left(- 3 e^{v} \sin{\left(u \right)}\right)^2 \\ &\quad+\left(- 3 e^{v} \cos{\left(u \right)}\right)^2\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\left\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\right\|&=\sqrt{e^{4 v} + 9 e^{2 v}} \\ &=\sqrt{\left(e^{2 v} + 9\right) e^{2 v}} \\ &=\sqrt{e^{2 v} + 9} e^{v}\end{aligned}
$$

Exponential factors are positive, so their squared factors have positive square roots.

Thus the required integral is

$$
A(S)=\iint_D \sqrt{e^{2 v} + 9} e^{v}\,\mathrm dA.
$$

The missing expression is $\sqrt{e^{2 v} + 9} e^{v}$. The integral does not need to be evaluated.

knowledge_point.title: Finding an Integral That Represents the Surface Area of a Parametric Surface

question.:question/problem:
$$
\iint_D\boxed{\phantom{AAAAAAAA}}\,\mathrm dA
$$

$$
D=\{(u,v):0\le u\le 2,\ 0\le v\le 4\}
$$

The integral above gives the surface area of the parametric surface

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\langle 3 u^{2},\,v^{2},\,u v\rangle
$$

for $(u,v)\in D$.

What is the missing expression?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The surface-area integrand is the magnitude of the fundamental vector product:

$$
A(S)=\iint_D \left\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\right\|\,\mathrm dA.
$$

Differentiate each coordinate with respect to each parameter:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u&=\langle 6 u,\,0,\,v\rangle \\ \mathbf r_v&=\langle 0,\,2 v,\,u\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Expand the determinant to find the cross product:

$$
\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i & \mathbf j & \mathbf k \\ 6 u & 0 & v \\ 0 & 2 v & u\end{vmatrix}
$$

$$
\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=\langle - 2 v^{2},\,- 6 u^{2},\,12 u v\rangle
$$

Square the components, add, and take the nonnegative square root:

$$
\begin{aligned}\left\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\right\|^2&=\left(- 2 v^{2}\right)^2+\left(- 6 u^{2}\right)^2 \\ &\quad+\left(12 u v\right)^2\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\left\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\right\|&=\sqrt{36 u^{4} + 144 u^{2} v^{2} + 4 v^{4}} \\ &=\sqrt{4 \left(9 u^{4} + 36 u^{2} v^{2} + v^{4}\right)} \\ &=2 \sqrt{9 u^{4} + 36 u^{2} v^{2} + v^{4}}\end{aligned}
$$

Thus the required integral is

$$
A(S)=\iint_D 2 \sqrt{9 u^{4} + 36 u^{2} v^{2} + v^{4}}\,\mathrm dA.
$$

The missing expression is $2 \sqrt{9 u^{4} + 36 u^{2} v^{2} + v^{4}}$. The integral does not need to be evaluated.
